key_insight: A local measurement-and-feedforward protocol can generate scalable graph states in quantum networks with amortized O(1) routing decisions, keeping classical delay far below qubit coherence times.
engineering_relevance: This is a practical architecture for fast, high-fidelity entanglement routing that could enable modular building blocks for fault-tolerant distributed quantum computing.
method: Use local measurements plus classical feedforward instead of global path computation.
Map the protocol onto a dual-species trapped-ion network model.
Apply hybrid simulation and an erasure transformation to suppress noise and improve star-subgraph fidelity.
evidence_signal: Hybrid simulations on the dual-species trapped-ion platform indicate good resource efficiency and time feasibility, with noise analysis showing readout fidelity as the main bottleneck.
watch_item: The approach still depends critically on improving readout fidelity and carefully managing multiplexing/branch independence in a real hardware implementation.
paper_title: Scalable Graph State Generation with O(1) Local Feedforward in Quantum Networks
